title: Responses API mapping: streaming & function-call parity gaps audit
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Background: Customers expect Redwood to behave like OpenAI's Responses API for streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. During model onboarding and customer migration we've observed subtle behavioral deltas that break client integrations (SDKs, browser apps, server side proxies). This ticket is an audit + mitigation plan to catalog gaps, propose concrete runtime and shim changes, and define acceptance criteria for parity-relevant behaviors.

Scope:
- Map event/stream formats (delta events, finalization events, role/name fields).
- Surface differences in tokenization/stream chunking semantics and consequences for client buffering and reassembly.
- Audit function/tool calling differences: invocation envelope, partial-argument streaming, deterministic finalization events, and error/fallback semantics.
- Structured output differences: JSON schema annotation, partial-emission of structured fields, and graceful failure modes when parse fails.
- Backwards compatibility: identify which deltas must be shimmed vs documented as deliberate behavior.

Deliverables:
1) Compatibility matrix (OpenAI Responses fields -> Redwood event fields) with category: Exact, Transformable, Needs shim, Not supported.
2) Test harness additions: simulated client reconstructor tests for chunk reassembly, function-call replay tests, schema-validation regression tests.
3) PR list: runtime changes, responses-adapter translation layer, and SDK changes (stream reassembly helpers).
4) Rollout plan: canary, staged release with telemetry gating and opt-in compatibility flag.

Acceptance criteria:
- For 90% of existing customer integrations (identified by telemetry and support tickets), behavior is either identical or documented with migration guidance.
- Streaming delta event mapping implemented for core event types: text.delta, tool_call.delta, tool_call.finish, structured_block.delta, and end-of-stream marker.
- Function call streaming: client sees tokens/args incrementally in same ordering as OpenAI; final function name/arguments event mirrors OpenAI's finalization envelope within 200ms wall-clock of final token emission in canary.
- Structured outputs: when model emits JSON-like chunks, SDK reconstructs and validates against provided schema; fallback behavior returns distinct error code and raw chunks when validation fails.

Non-goals: deep behavioral parity for every historic minor edge-case (we will triage those into follow-ups), matching downstream OpenAI telemetry payloads exactly (we will provide mapping, not identical instrumentation).
comments: 2025-02-11 - Diego Martínez: Initial spike complete. Found three canonical streaming deltas: 'text.delta' that conflates role/name in some models, 'function_call.delta' which in OpenAI includes incremental 'arguments' tokens plus a terminal 'function_call' event, and a separate 'structured' block mechanism. Need to standardize Redwood event names and mapping rules.

2025-02-13 - Ava Thompson: Design review notes - prefer a translation layer approach (responses-adapter) that normalizes incoming model/runtime events into a stable Responses-compatible wire format. Avoid touching model-serving kernels for first pass to reduce risk.

2025-02-17 - Priya Rao (PM): Customer impact ranking completed; 12 accounts affected by streaming ordering differences, 3 enterprise customers rely on token-level function arg streaming for real-time UI. Recommend prioritizing streaming and function-call shim for canary.

2025-02-19 - Diego Martínez: Added prototype adapter in github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/responses-adapter/pull/82 (WIP). Prototype normalizes: role/name fields, emits explicit 'delta_type' header, and reconstructs 'function_call' finish envelope. Needs stress testing for throughput implications.

2025-02-22 - Security review: briefed security on potential leakage via function-call args streaming. KMS/HSM unaffected but recommended review of logs retention for delta chunks. Security flagged audit logging requirement for enterprise customers.

2025-02-25 - QA: Draft test plan created in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RESP/Responses+Interop+Test+Plan. Includes unit tests for chunk reassembly, end-to-end canary harness, and fuzz tests for malformed partial-JSON emissions.

2025-02-28 - Diego Martínez: Performance note - adapter adds ~1.8% CPU overhead in microbenchmarks for small responses but can increase memory pressure on large concurrent streaming workloads. Investigating streaming passthrough optimizations and zero-copy buffer mapping.

2025-02-28 - Ava Thompson: Next: finalize compatibility matrix, land adapter PR with feature flag off by default, start canary for 5% of small-hosted traffic with telemetry checks (error rates, reassembly failures).
